in_english.name: Mughith
in_english.meaning: blessed with abundant life, preventer of evil, giver of prosperity, bringer of good fortune, successful in good deeds
in_english.long_meaning: The name Mughith is derived from the Arabic root 'M-G-Th', which means to bless with abundant life, to prevent evil, to give prosperity, to bring good fortune, and to be successful in good deeds. It is mentioned in the Quran as a name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. In Islamic tradition, Mughith is considered a name that conveys blessings, prosperity, and good fortune.

historical_references.reference: Mughith ad-Din Muhammad ibn Bahadur was a Sultan of the Deccan Sultanate of the Bahmani dynasty. He ruled from 1422 to 1435 CE and is best known for his military conquests and patronage of architecture and learning. He expanded the Bahmani sultanate's territories, defeating Rashtrakutas and Vijayanagara forces.
historical_references.context: Sultan of the Deccan Sultanate of the Bahmani dynasty

historical_references.reference: Mughith Shah, also known as Mughith Al-Din Muhammad, was a Sultan of the Ghaznavid Empire from 1131 to 1148 CE. He was the eldest son of Bhaktiyar Khawar, and succeeded his father upon his death. Mughith Shah is remembered for his military victories against the Seljuks, Khurramites, and Khwarazmian Shia rebels.
